subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jmiller@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to get a sense of FinBot's priorities and constraints. Below is a short recap from our discussion and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please flag anything I missed or that you'd like reworded.

Key pain points you shared
- Unit economics: token costs and GPU spend are the top gating factor for expansion (especially during peak morning batch windows).
- Unpredictable per-request cost: spikes from tail-latency and retries are driving unexpected overages.
- Lack of model-optimized infra: current infra doesn't use KV caching or quantization; batching is conservative because of latency concerns.

Current stack (as described)
- Inference hosted on GCP (NVIDIA A10p / T4 fleet) with autoscaling via Kubernetes.
- Model: open LLM (name TBD) run in FP16; no quantization in prod.
- No prefix/KV caching for repeated context; end-to-end latency targets are aggressive for user-facing features (~p95 < 300ms).

Success criteria for a trial with Redwood
- Reduce per-1k-token inference cost by ~2.5–3x while keeping user-observed latency within +-50ms of current baseline (p95 target <= 300ms).
- Demonstrate stable tail-latency under morning surge (2x traffic).
- Run a short quality check (1000 prompts) pre/post quantization to ensure no regression in LLM output.

Openness and constraints
- Quantization: team is open to 8-bit and 4-bit trials but will require a quality gate.
- Batching: acceptable to introduce small batch-waits if p95 stays within target (you mentioned batching up to ~50ms is OK for some routes).
- Data/privacy: must stay within existing compliance boundary (no external PII export).

Next steps (proposed)
1) You to share FinBot traffic profile and a small sample of non-sensitive prompts (we can use synthetic if needed).
2) Redwood to propose a trial configuration (model variant + batching/caching + quantization profile) and estimated unit economics.
3) Schedule a 45-min technical call next week with Ben (inference lead) to review the proposed runtime plan.
4) Optional: sign an NDA/preview SOW if you want us to run a short dedicated-capacity trial.

Attachments: I attached the traffic sample you sent earlier and a short pricing/assumptions worksheet for model-profile estimation.

Thanks — I'll coordinate Calendly slots for the tech call if you're available next week.

Best,
Marissa
